trailheadDirection: From Glacier, drive SR 542 east about 24 miles to the end of the highway at the large Artist Point parking lot.
approach: Reach this climb on skis from the Artist Point Trailhead. Skin up to Herman Saddle, then traverse out beneath the west face of Table Mountain across a steep slope that can slide. Near the middle of the face, look for a shallow cleft with linked patches of ice; the climb starts there.
note: MP route page for approach; area page and WTA for the lot and drive.

approach: From the Artist Point Trailhead, ski across to the foot of the east face of Table Mountain, where an obvious cleft splits the face. The climb begins by entering that cleft on steep snow.
note: MP route page for approach; area page and WTA for the lot and drive.

trailhead: Dingford Creek Trailhead (Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road)
trailheadDirection: From I-90 exit 34 near North Bend, follow 468th to Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road, turn right and drive 12 miles, passing the large Middle Fork parking area on the right. Cross the large concrete bridge, immediately turn right onto the gravel road signed for Dingford and Dutch Miller Gap, and follow it about 6 miles to the gate and trailhead.
approach: From the Dingford Creek Trailhead (Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road), take the trail toward Myrtle and Hester Lakes and go east at the junction on the Hester Lake trail. Leave the trail near 3,360 ft and climb a brushy basin to the east, then turn north near 4,000 ft up the west side of a large avalanche chute. Reach a meadow at 4,920 ft, cross to a ridge and follow it north through alpine meadows toward the summit.
note: One trip log of a scramble on the peak that matches the Hester Lake start; not confirmed as this ridge.

trailheadDirection: From the Nisqually entrance of Mount Rainier National Park, drive east on Paradise Road about 14 miles; the signed Narada Falls parking lot is on the right, about 1 mile before the Paradise area.
approach: From the Narada Falls trailhead/parking, in winter and spring cross the footbridge, then climb the slope to the closed Stevens Canyon Road. At the bend in the road, head southwest into the woods and drop to the Tatoosh Creek drainage, crossing the creek where it is safe. Continue toward the north face; The Fly is the westernmost and gentlest of its three couloirs, and it starts from the base of the face at roughly 5,000 ft.
note: MP route page Location; area page agrees on Narada Falls as the cold-season start.

trailhead: Eldorado Creek trailhead (Cascade River Road mile 20)
trailheadDirection: From Marblemount, go straight past the last gas station onto Cascade River Road, cross the bridge and drive to the Eldorado Creek trailhead at mile 20, on the right; the last 10 miles are gravel.
approach: From the Eldorado Creek trailhead (Cascade River Road mile 20), cross the stream on logs and follow a faint trail through boulders to a talus field near 4,000 ft. Continue to an open basin at 5,400 ft, cross the left-hand ridge near 6,000 ft, and drop down a third-class gully into the Roush Creek basin. Climb the Eldorado Glacier to where it levels near 7,500 ft, then gain the East Ridge. Traverse at about 8,100 ft to the north side, to the notch before the first rock spire, rappel into the west-facing cirque and head south to the couloir, which starts at about 7,800 ft.
note: NW couloir page gives its own start; East Ridge page gives the trailhead-to-glacier approach.

trailheadDirection: From Marblemount, drive SR-20 east about 45 miles and turn right between mileposts 151 and 152 onto the signed Easy Pass road, which leads to the trailhead lot.
approach: From the Easy Pass (#741) trailhead, follow the Easy Pass trail and traverse the slopes across to Mesahchie Col. Scramble down north onto the Mesahchie Glacier and traverse left across it to the base of the Icefall Couloir, where the climb begins.
note: MP route Location and area page agree; drive matches the area page.

trailheadDirection: From Trout Lake, drive Mt. Adams Road north about 1.3 miles, then turn left onto Forest Road 23 (Buck Creek Road) and follow it about 17.5 miles to the trailhead, which is easy to miss between mileposts 38 and 37.
approach: From the Riley Camp Trailhead, hike the Riley Camp Trail, staying off the Riley Cut-Off at the first junction, until it meets the Pacific Crest Trail. Turn south on the Pacific Crest Trail for a few minutes to Riley Creek and follow the creek up through boulders to the moraines at the foot of the Pinnacle Glacier. The headwall route begins at the base of the glacier.
note: MP route names Riley trailhead; trip log gives the creek-to-glacier line; WTA gives the drive. Glacier-base start inferred.

trailheadDirection: From I-90 exit 52 at Snoqualmie Pass, drive to the Alpental ski area parking at the end of Alpental Road, and respect any no-parking requests near the private homes.
approach: From the Alpental / Snow Lake Trailhead (I-90 Exit 52), take the Snow Lake trail to Gem Lake, ford the outlet and pick up a boot path on the northeast ridge. Near a talus field at about 5,500 ft, leave the ridge toward the south side and make a descending traverse beneath a cliff band. Past the cliffs, climb one of two gullies to a basin at about 5,600 ft between the true summit and the north summit, then go southeast up a ramp to the steep heather slope below the top.
note: One trip log of the line to the true summit; WTA for the Exit 52 / Alpental parking.

trailheadDirection: From Leavenworth, drive US-2 west 0.8 mile, turn left onto Icicle Road for about 8.5 miles, then turn left onto Eightmile Road (FR-7600), stay right onto FR-7601 and follow it about 4 miles to the trailhead. The last stretch closes in winter, typically November to May.
approach: From the Stuart Lake Trailhead (Trail #1599), follow the main path until it forks and bear right for Stuart Lake. After about a quarter mile, drop to the creek and find the climbers path, then keep east of Mountaineers Ridge and ascend talus or steep snow to the upper valley and the campsites near 5,400 ft below the Sherpa Glacier. The Ice Cliff Glacier, which this route climbs, lies between the Sherpa Glacier and the North Ridge.
note: Approach from the neighbouring Ice Cliff Glacier page (same glacier start); this route's page names the NE face and the glacier but gives no approach.

trailheadDirection: From Glacier, drive SR 542 east about 12.5 miles to Hannegan Pass Road (FR 32) and turn left. After a little over 1 mile, turn onto Nooksack Cirque Road (FR 34) and follow it about 1 mile to the parking area at the road's end.
approach: From the Nooksack Cirque Trailhead (Trail #750), follow the trail and an old railbed to the Nooksack River and ford it. Bushwhack for hours to the moraine, then climb steeply through brush to the ridge and traverse to rock slabs, a usual bivy spot. Continue to a notch near 5,900 ft, make a single rappel onto the glacier, cross it and end-run a crevasse to reach the foot of the steep snow gully where the route starts.
note: One 2024 trip report of this route; WTA for the drive.

trailheadDirection: From Leavenworth, drive US-2 west 0.8 mile, turn left onto Icicle Road for about 8.5 miles, then turn left onto Eightmile Road (FR-7600), stay right onto FR-7601 and follow it about 4 miles to the trailhead. The last stretch closes in winter, typically November to May.
approach: From the Stuart Lake Trailhead (Trail #1599), hike to Colchuck Lake, work around it and climb the steep trail to Aasgard Pass. From the pass head south to southwest uphill toward Witches Tower; the north side shows a dark steep wall.
note: Describes the approach to the peak only, not this buttress.
